label: ACP is a stdio JSON-RPC agent with initialize, authenticate, new_session, load_session, prompt, cancel and close_session; vibe-acp takes only -h, -v and --setup, so behaviour is protocol and config driven.
ACP carries permission round-trips via client.request_permission with allow_once, allow_always, reject_once and reject_always, unlike print mode which denies a tool that needs approval.
ACP sessions are persistent and cancellable: new_session, load_session, close_session and cancel let one process hold many sessions, resume them and stop a turn without dying.
ACP has no per-run exit taxonomy and no export.json; outcome, usage and cost are print-mode artifacts an ACP supervisor must reconstruct from protocol events.

Three further seams exist: --output streaming for an event stream, --agent-socket for server-owned abort (exit 4), and run-server for many headless runs over JSON-RPC (experimental) with --runs-per-app-server.

Print mode fits the existing executor contract with no new supervisor; ACP would need a persistent per-lineage client, a protocol-derived completion signal, a permission answerer, cancellation semantics and session-anchored receipts.
Recommendation: print mode is the better first dispatch surface, ACP the better second one once a supervisor can answer permissions and resume, and run-server waits until it leaves experimental.

ACP would change four fan-out mechanics: one process per lineage instead of per iteration, a new per-iteration completion record, a per-lineage permission answerer, and cancellation mapped onto existing signal handlers.
